member of the commission. - the madam president, i would like to point out that the fundamental principle of european union food law is that only safe food is placed on the community market, and all food and feed lawfully placed on the european union market must be safe regardless of its origin. a wide range of measures to ensure food safety and facilitate the withdrawal of unsafe food and feed from the market have been introduced in community legislation. the general food regulation requires traceability in the european union to be compulsory for food businesses at all levels and stages of the food chain, from importers to retailers. with regard in particular to products of animal origin, including products originating in third countries, food hygiene legislation further strengthens the traceability rules for products of animal origin covered by regulation (ec) no 853/2004 through the following requirements: food business operators must have systems and procedures in place to identify the food business operators from whom they have received and to whom they have delivered products of animal origin. these products must also bear a mark of suitability or an identification mark. the commission does not foresee any changes to the traceability rules and the fitness or identification marking for processed food of animal origin. as regards the compulsory indication of the place of origin of all foodstuffs in general, it should be stressed that the indication of the origin of foodstuffs is not a means of ensuring food safety but a tool by which the citizen is informed of the characteristics of each product. however, indication of the place of origin is required in principle in cases where there is a risk of misleading consumers as to the true origin or provenance of foodstuffs, and also in the application of specific rules such as those relating to fruit, vegetables, beef, wine, honey and fish. in such cases, the marking of origin is compulsory. indication of origin is also required for imported poultrymeat and, from 1 july 2010, for pre-packaged food labelled as organic. in such cases, the indication of origin is necessary and obligatory. the commission is aware, of course, that this is a matter which requires further discussion and we know that citizens often ask to know the origin of products. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural products are labelled in the community's official language, and that the community's agricultural products are labelled in the official language. the labelling of foodstuffs may of course be voluntary rather than compulsory, but in this case we must follow certain common rules so that all member states comply. the commission proposal on food in food, should also be given to the buyer during the distance selling; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the quality of the products is not affected by the quality madam president, a particularly significant number of counterfeit products trafficked via the internet or the legitimate supply chain are counterfeit medicinal products. the health risks to patients who take them unknowingly are obvious. these products are manufactured in factories or laboratories that do not follow the rules of good manufacturing practice and in many cases do not contain any trace of the therapeutic active substance. in a recent statement, president kovács said that in the last two months, checks by customs authorities in european union countries have found more than 34 million tablets of antibiotics, oncology and other falsified medicines. is it not time, commissioner, for the european union to open in china and india, for example, export monitoring offices in line with the fda standards, which opened such offices last month? and you should know that without the mandatory cooperation of the pharmaceutical agencies of these countries there is no way to control the 3,000 pharmaceutical factories in india and the 12,000 factories in china.
the commission's vice-president - madam president, first of all, of course, i listened very carefully to all the speeches. i shall report to my colleague, mr charlie mccreevy, of course, who is in charge of the internal market. i think that parliament has appreciated the seriousness of the phenomenon and its effects, which jacques toubon has called a scourge of economic, social and health concern. it is clear that the european union, while open to trade, cannot accept that trade be conducted in violation of the basic rules of the game and to the detriment of consumers. so we must do something right and i would like to recall a number of things. firstly, and i am responding in particular to mr toubon, the european observatory on counterfeiting and piracy will be launched by the commission in spring 2009. the observatory is to provide statistics on counterfeiting and piracy in the internal market. the observatory should identify vulnerable geographical areas and the illicit trafficking of websites selling counterfeit goods. it must also organise administrative cooperation between the member states, organise the exchange of information and, as mr martin said, raise consumer awareness. this is a major task for this observatory. it is true that the criminal provisions were proposed by the commission in 2006, and we have the support of parliament, but at the moment the council is not yet involved in the adoption of the criminal provisions. in this respect, cooperation should not only concern customs but also the police, the judicial authorities and, in general, all those who can intervene in the monitoring and control of such falsification. i would like to say to those who have insisted on the need for indications indicating the origin of products that we have proposed a made in and that this made in has not yet been adopted by the council. the european union must not be afraid of this display, which will allow consumers to make their own judgments and avoid being the victim of practices that are totally contrary to all the rules of the game. i would add that acta cannot be accused of going further than the current eu regime for the enforcement of intellectual property rights, and in particular of violating fundamental freedoms and the protection of personal data. acta remains within the framework of the current regime of the european union. in any case, i thank parliament for its willingness to join the commission in trying to achieve an effective fight against counterfeiting. we take note of this report and we also take note of the european parliament's determination to combat this system effectively. i may not have answered all the questions. there are also products which can be described as similar, and we must also have rules to prevent abuse, which is absolutely reprehensible and detrimental to the consumer. that is what i wanted to say in conclusion, but i want you to know that all the remarks made tonight will be brought to the attention of the commissioners because, again, this is a complex matter which requires the implementation of several commission guidelines and which also requires a full commitment from the council and from parliament.
the joint debate is closed. the vote will take place tomorrow, 18 december 2008.
mr president, e-justice – electronic justice – can we say that such a thing is possible in an activity that is conditioned by human weaknesses and virtues, which are very human characteristics? no! can there be borderless justice? as you said, no, again! because this is a human activity, which is also very different in every part of the world. do those two ‘nos’ mean that we must turn our back on technological innovation? again, of course, no! we must try to exploit human innovation. a portal for information: yes! exchange of data: yes! awareness of the interindependence of the judicial systems: yes! contribution to the creation of a european demos: yes! but for common faceless justice – and i do not say that you are doing that in your report – no! my father, who was a judge, would not be too eager for me to defend electronic justice before the european parliament. if i myself speak from the european parliament to my father, who is in heaven, i can tell him that i know that justice will always be a man, his defender and a judge – not before god but before their conscience.
the rapporteur. - the mr president, ladies and gentlemen, until now, crossborder trade in aeronautical equipment has been subject to legal uncertainties. the new international legal framework aims to facilitate the provision of financing for the acquisition of aeronautical equipment, i.e. aircraft, engines and parts, by establishing a particularly strong international guarantee in favour of the lenders, i.e. credit dealers or organisations financing the acquisition of the equipment in question. overall, the new legal regime will reduce the cost of financing aviation equipment worldwide and contribute to savings of billions of euros per year in the aviation sector. finally, the positive impact of the most advanced regulatory framework in the history of aviation financial law is not only for financial operators and manufacturers but also for airlines, employees and passengers.
the next item is the debate on six motions for resolutions on zimbabwe. i 'm not .
the commission's vice-president - madam president, i thank all the members who have made an urgent appeal for zimbabwe, because zimbabwe is facing a crisis of unprecedented magnitude that is getting worse, not a single sector is spared. at the political level, we are witnessing an increase in violence, as evidenced by reports of arbitrary arrests and the disappearance of human rights activists. the increase in political violence can make any solution to the crisis impossible and push the parties towards irreconcilable positions. the humanitarian situation is deteriorating, as evidenced by the cholera epidemic that is spreading and threatening zimbabwe's neighbouring countries. the economic situation is dire. prices of basic commodities continue to rise. the cost of the average grocery basket has increased by 1,293% in the last week. at the social level, the risks of an explosion are increasing day by day, with the possible negative effect on the stability of the whole region. so what can we do? the needs of zimbabwe are enormous. they are increasing exponentially mainly because of the mismanagement of the current government. the commission is continuing its active involvement in humanitarian matters. a field mission, from 15 to 19 december, is reassessing the humanitarian situation, which will allow us, among other things, to identify very quickly any additional needs. at the political level, the commission - and beyond that the international community as a whole - can only help zimbabwe if it can work closely with a legitimate government with sufficient leeway to adopt the necessary political and economic measures. this requires the implementation of the agreement of 15 september and the establishment of a government of national unity. this also requires increased involvement of the actors in the region and the african union. we are very much looking forward to this involvement in all our contacts with them. i can assure you that the commission, which is following the situation on the ground very closely, is continuing to work with all the member states, the african and international partners, in the search for a just solution that will allow zimbabwe to emerge from the current crisis which you have both strongly denounced. thank you very much for your attention, and it is true that during this holiday season, we cannot forget all those people who are suffering in zimbabwe. they are perhaps among the most distressed people in the world today.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place after the debate.
the next item is the debate on six motions for resolutions on nicaragua. i 'm not .
the commission's vice-president - madam president, the political situation in nicaragua has worsened with the approach of the local elections on 9 november. the numerous appeals for calm from the international community, and in particular from the european union and commission missions, have been ignored. after the vote, the circumstances surrounding the count and the announcement of the results gave rise to a crisis with the main opposition party. the liberal constitutionalist party rejects the results and denounces massive fraud. citizen movements, the church and business associations, the international community have called for the results to be reviewed or for new elections to be held. the political institutions, and in particular the parliament, have also been blocked by the lack of agreement between the two main parties. the reports of our heads of mission on the ground and the report of the electoral experts seconded by the commission have reported violations of electoral laws and international conventions. in agreement with the member states and after consulting other partners, the commission sent a letter to the nicaraguan authorities on 10 december offering its support for any concerted solution between the country's political forces to overcome the crisis and restore citizens' confidence in democratic institutions. the letter also announced the suspension of disbursements from budget support programmes as from 1 january 2009 and the opening of a period of consultation with the nicaraguan authorities on the current situation and the modalities for reorienting european cooperation with the country. i should also point out that the commission has not withdrawn its 2008 aid to nicaragua €20 million has been distributed, including emergency humanitarian aid and everything that was planned for this year will be paid as long as the conditions inherent in each project are met. the budget support of eur 57 million for 2009 is not withdrawn but suspended. cooperation will be directed towards programmes and activities that ensure that aid reaches the beneficiaries, the nicaraguan people, directly, without going through the government. i would add that the foreign minister, mr samuel santos, in a letter to commissioner ferrero-waldner on 12 december, expressed his disagreement with the measure. it reaffirmed the validity of the results and expressed its readiness for a dialogue on cooperation which the commission intends to launch as soon as possible. finally, in response to one of the speakers, i would say that the commission naturally hopes that the current crisis will be resolved as soon as possible and, in any event, the eu-central america association agreement repeatedly emphasizes the importance attached by the parties to respect for democratic principles and values and good governance. the negotiations on this association agreement will provide an opportunity to deepen the discussion on these principles, including their application in practice. i am able to give you this information, and i know that mrs ferrero-waldner is following the situation very closely with the commission services. i thank you and all the speakers for your kindness in bringing up the situation in nicaragua.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place after the debate. the court of justice shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine the appeal.
the next item is the debate on six motions for resolutions on russia.
the commission's vice-president - madam president, on 5 november, president medvedev, in his first annual address to the federation council, explicitly mentioned the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms. this symbolic mention, in this year of the anniversary of the universal declaration, is a testimony to the new president's interest in judicial reform and its impact on human rights. the european union will have to follow developments in this area very closely. the reality of the past few weeks has once again reminded us of the great challenges facing human rights defenders in russia. we have listened carefully, of course, to the various speakers, madam president, who have not failed to point out the serious threats to human rights in russia. two years after her death, the murder trial in the case of anna politkovskaya began. it was first open to the public, then held behind closed doors, then reopened to the public. the trial will be closely watched by all those who defend freedom of speech. as the murder of magomed yevloyev in police custody in late august reminded us, journalism in russia is becoming an increasingly dangerous profession. in early december, memorial, one of the oldest and most prestigious ngos working on the painful past of 20th century russia, was raided by police. the result of this search was the confiscation of the historical archives of the gulag. if we really want to continue the work we started last april at the conference on the crimes of totalitarian regimes in europe - a conference which i myself opened - then it goes without saying that historians must have access to the archives. the december 4 raid is a disturbing message to those who believe in the need for debate, and honest debate, about the deep wounds of the past. this debate is necessary to ensure the necessary reconciliations in the future. of course, the consultations between the european union and russian human rights authorities are an opportunity to remind the need to respect the commitments that russia has made in the field of human rights. the commission continues its work in support of civil society initiatives, in particular through the european initiative for democracy and human rights. support for judicial reform is also a priority in our cooperation programmes with russia. i have been in contact with the new judicial officials at the last meeting with russia and i intend to continue a demanding dialogue. the european union and russia are also currently negotiating a new contractual basis to replace the current partnership and cooperation agreement. of course, respect for human rights must be an essential element of this new agreement. the commitments made by the parties in the context of the un, the organisation for security and cooperation in europe or the council of europe must be implemented; the commission remains committed to this. mrs ferrero-waldner asked me to thank you for introducing this debate and confirmed her personal commitment. i would add my own, since i have the opportunity, in the field of security and justice, to be able to hold a dialogue with the moscow authorities. i can say this, madam president: i hope that 2010 will be an opportunity for russian officials to be able to fulfil their commitments better than they have done this year.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place immediately. the court of justice shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine the appeal.
